findings.claim: The checklist pin sets display, box-sizing, width, min-width, max-width, padding, border, transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom with inline !important, but not transition. Transition declarations sit above important author declarations in the cascade, so if a learner's stylesheet gives .site-aside a transition covering width (for example transition: all .3s, harmless page polish), the second pin (480px to 720px in the same window) animates from its start value at the moment the test reads offsetWidth. Reproduced in pinned Chromium: the private completed work plus only that one aside transition rule fails task 11 (11 pass, 1 fail) with the fill-the-checklist message reporting the tag at 480px when the checklist is 720px wide, which wrongly tells the learner to remove a wrapper, float, columns or positioning. Box model and own widths are correct, so this is a false fail with a misleading message. Low because nothing in the lab asks for a transition on the aside. A second variant fails the same way on the tag side: the completed work plus interpolate-size: allow-keywords on :root and a width transition on .pack-tag fails task 11 on the control, because the temporary width: auto now animates and the test reads the tag at its old size. Also low: interpolate-size is new and unlikely in a beginner page.

evidence.section: 6.1 Cascade Sorting Order (Origin and Importance: transition declarations precede important author declarations)

findings.recommendation: Neutralise transitions and animations during measurement on both sides: add transition: none and animation: none to the pinned() map for .site-aside, and set them inline !important on each tag before the control (restoring afterwards), or read the pinned and released widths back and assert they took effect before asserting on the tags.

findings.claim: box-sizing is asserted only on runs[0] (800px window, 480px checklist). README line 17 says the test measures each tag's box-sizing and lab.json notes list box-sizing among the measured items, implying it holds in every case. Reproduced: the private completed work plus a rule that, only from a 1000px window, switches .pack-tag-day to border-box with the width that model needs passes all 12 tests, although at 1280px the day tag no longer uses content-box. The 800px case still forces the content-box calculation, so the objective is still practised; the gap is that the stated per-case box-sizing check is not enforced.

evidence.section: 3.3 Box Edges for Sizing: the box-sizing property

findings.recommendation: Move the two box-sizing assertions inside the for (const run of runs) loop so each of the four cases checks content-box for .pack-tag-day and border-box for .pack-tag-overnight.

findings.claim: README says task 11 'rejects scaling, rotating, moving or zooming a tag', but the test rejects only the transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom properties on the tag (lab.json notes state this accurately). A tag moved with position: relative and a left offset passes all 12 tests (reproduced). Similarly, Outcome line 141 says the tags stay 'ordinary blocks directly in the gear checklist', yet an unpadded wrapper div around both tags, and absolutely positioned tags with zero left and right insets inside a positioned checklist, both pass all 12 (reproduced): the control rejects only arrangements whose auto width would not fill the checklist. None of these lets the 200px skip the calculation, so the narrowing is safe and the Troubleshooting text describes the failing case correctly; only the README's description of what is rejected is broader than the test.
findings.recommendation: Say 'It rejects scaling, rotating, translating or zooming a tag' in README line 17 (matching lab.json), and optionally say in Troubleshooting that the control fails when anything around the tag stops it filling the checklist, rather than implying every wrapper or positioning fails.

findings.claim: The solved-run record's core claims verify on current bytes (commit 0e12a9f7, all 13 artifactHashes equal the lab bytes at 0e12a9f7 and at 78b53ccb, starter 0/12, completed 12/12, timing-masked output matches expected/on-completion.txt). But two fields carried over from the earlier record are now false for this run: 'contract' (line 8) says it was 'exercised on a fresh pep export-lab bundle' while procedure line 17 says the lab was taken with git archive into a private directory; and 'privateStaging' (line 28) says the solution 'existed only in the private $TMPDIR copy of the export during the run' while 'cleanup' (line 27) says the private copy stays in uncommitted private staging. The record therefore contradicts itself about how the run was made and what remains. Unconfirmed rather than false: environment.os is unchanged from the earlier record (Darwin 25.6.0), while the host this critic ran on reports Darwin 27.2.0; the record does not say which host made run clean-loop3-1795052566, so the OS line may be stale.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite 'contract' and 'privateStaging' to describe this run (git archive of the lab at 0e12a9f7 into private staging; the completed files and node_modules remain only in uncommitted private staging), or rerun from a pep export-lab bundle and record that instead. Update environment.os to the host that actually made this run.

findings.claim: Earlier concern 5 (a viewport-unit width passing because the page was opened at one window size) partly recurs. The test changes the window width (800, 1280) but keeps the window height at 800 in both runs, so a width in height-based viewport units resolves to the same length in all four cases. Reproduced: the private completed work with .pack-tag-overnight's width replaced by a vh value that equals 200px at an 800px-high window passes all 12 tests, and the same with a vmin value also passes 12/12 (at both test windows the height is the smaller side). In a real browser window of another height the tag is not 200px wide. The README Troubleshooting line 'A width that depends on the window or on the space around the tag fails when the test changes those sizes' is therefore false for vh, vmin and similar height-based units. The control does not catch this because the tag still fills the checklist once its own width is removed. The same applies to the content-box tag with a vh value of the calculated width. Medium rather than high because a learner would have to pick height units on purpose, and the content-box case still needs the calculation.
findings.recommendation: Vary the window height as well as the width between the two runs (for example a short window and a tall one, with the narrow/wide and short/tall pairings chosen so vw, vh, vmin and vmax each change), and add a vh/vmin variant to the solved-run matrix.
